caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.462 of 1995.
lawyer:
MA Mannan, Advocate, Instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioners. 
Not Represented — Respondent.
parties:
Tara Miah (Md) and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Bhovotush Das  ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarker J: Predecessor of respondent No. 1 instituted Title Suit No. 172 of 1974 as the sole plaintiff in the First Court of Munsif, Sylhet against the predecessor of the petitioners, Abdul Bari, for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction in the suit land. After filing the suit on the prayer of the plaintiff the learned Munsif granted temporary injunction restraining the defendant from interfering with the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. Thereafter the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No. 304 of 1974 under Order XXXIX, rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure against the defendant alleging violation of the Court's order and the learned Munsif by his order dated 3-6-1980 passed an order for attachment of the property of the defendant for one year. The defendant thereafter preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 159 of 1980 in the Court of District Judge, Sylhet and the records of the case was called for in connection with the appeal which was lying in the appellate Court. 

 2. During the pendency of the Miscellaneous Appeal the sole plaintiff, Surabala Das died on 14-4-1983 but the defendant appellant did not take any step for substitution of her heirs. Then on an application made by the learned Advocate for the deceased plaintiff-respondent, the appellate Court by an order dated 1-1-1985 recorded an order of abatement of the Miscellaneous appeal and sent down the record to the trial Court. In the meantime the sole defendant died on 25-1-1985. 

 4. Mr. MA Mannan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners has submitted that the sole plaintiff having died on 14-4-1983 and no application for substitution having been made within time and without any application for condonation of delay, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in upholding the order of the substitution passed by the learned Munsif. The learned Advocate also submitted that the order of the learned Munsif allowing substitution of the heirs in place of the deceased defendant was also bad in law for the same reasons. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division noticed that although the sole plaintiff died during the pendency of the miscellaneous appeal filed by the sole defendant, it was incumbent upon him to substitute the heirs of the deceased plaintiff in the miscellaneous appeal. 

 5. The record of the case was received by the trial Court in May 1986 and the learned Munsif by his order, dated 10-7-1986 directed to inform the lawyers of both sides. Respondent No.1 filed the application for his substitution in place of the sole plaintiff on 14-6-1986 which was fixed for hearing on 16-9-1986 and on that date respondent No.1 filed another application for substitution of the petitioners in place of the deceased defendant who died on 25-1-1985 when the record of the case was still in the appellate Court. 

 It appears that although respondent 1 filed the application without any prayer for setting aside abatement and without any application of condemnation of delay he filed the applications within reasonable time of the receipt of the record by the trial Court and the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division observed that "this circumstance for non-filing of application in time may also be construed as an application under Order 22 rule 9(2) of the CPC". Further, relying upon two decisions of the High Court Division, the learned Judge treated both the applications under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, in the facts and circumstances of the case. We find that the learned Single Judge has committed no illegality calling for any interference by this Division. This petition is, therefore, dismissed.
